newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No tariff cuts in Singapore - chemical industry.
newsitem.headline: No tariff cuts in Singapore - chemical industry.

text.p: The European chemical industry said on Thursday it would oppose any further tariff reductions at the ministerial meeting of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in Singapore in December.

The European Chemical Industry Council (CEFIC) said the industry, having agreed to harmonise all chemical tariffs at a low level during the tariff-cutting Uruguay Round, had shown its commitment to liberalisation.

But it had been disappointed that not all major chemical producing countries had joined the Chemical Tariff Harmonisation Agreement and "in view of this, CEFIC is against any further tariff reductions at Singapore," it said in a statement.
The industry would nevertheless "support the total elimination of chemical tariffs by 2010 provided this was accepted by all WTO members."

David Wakeford, chairman of CEFIC's external trade committee, said the European chemical industry sees the overwhelming priority as consolidation and strengthening of the multilateral trading system through full implementation of the Uruguay Round.
CEFIC said there should be an opportunity for the Singapore meeting to maintain the momentum of liberalisation by adopting a few focused initiatives.
"Simplification and standardisation of customs procedures would address one of the biggest non-tariff barriers to international trade," it said.
